name: Northern and Yorke Landscape Board Bite-sized Grants
summary: Small, short-term grants for community groups and not-for-profits in South Australia's Northern and Yorke landscape region, for work such as weed control, revegetation and pest animal management.

eligibility.rule: Have public liability insurance or an insured incorporated sponsor that manages the grant
Be a legal entity or have a sponsor that is a legal entity
Not be an individual landholder, unless part of a group of 3 or more with an incorporated sponsor
Align all funded activities with Landscape Board priorities
Have no environmentally damaging, new agricultural production or profit-making activities
Have no outstanding final report or financial acquittal from a previous grant round
Receive at most one Bite-sized Grant per financial year. Unsuccessful applicants may reapply.

documents: Sponsor letter accepting legal and financial responsibility, if sponsored

deadline.text: 5pm on Friday 30 April 2027 or until funds are expended

applicant_types.quote: Funding of between $200 and $2,000 is available for community groups and not-for-profit organisations for small, short-term projects.

window.quote: The 2026-2027 round of the Bite-sized Grants program opens Friday 28 August 2026.

amount.quote: Funding of between $200 and $2,000 is available for community groups and not-for-profit organisations for small, short-term projects.

effort.quote: Applications open on Friday 28 August 2026 and close on 5pm on Friday 30 April 2027 or until funds are expended.
Applications are assessed by a small committee and when needed, specialist advisors.

eligibility.quote: If you / your organisation does not have public liability insurance, an incorporated organisation meeting these requirements must sponsor your application and manage the grant on your behalf.
All applicants are required to be either a 'legal entity' as listed below or have a sponsor who is a 'legal entity':
Individual landholders cannot apply, although groups of 3 or more landholders may apply with the support of an incorporated sponsor such as a Local Government or ag bureau)

All activities funded by a Bite-sized Grant must align with the priorities of the Landscape Board which includes, pest plant and animal control, water management and water course health, protecting or conserving biodiversity, First Nations engagement and support, and sustainable agriculture practices.

activities that are causing or likely to cause environmental damage, either directly or indirectly establishment of new agricultural production sites or facilities activities that would create beneficial monetary profits for the applicant or sponsoring body
If a final report and financial acquittal is outstanding from a previous round of grant program funding, the grantee will be considered ineligible to submit a grant application.
A group may only receive funding once per financial year, however a group may reapply if their application was unsuccessful.

after_award.quote: Projects must be completed, funds acquitted, and a report submitted within 3 months of receiving the grant.
You will be required to report on these activities in your interim and final reports.

documents.quote: Please upload a letter from your sponsor confirming their willingness to accept legal and financial responsibility for the project if successful.
